concrete_capability_transition: CLI run preconditions corrected: objective text after the run command is preserved losslessly, read-only and objective-execution transport timeout classes are separated, and CLI Product DoD acceptance now assigns advertised mode/list and bounded JSON/list requirements before product completion.

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Removes concrete blockers to safe CLI objective execution by preserving arbitrary objective tokens and preventing read-only transport timeouts from governing long-running runtime execution calls.

Keeps execution budgets, LLM/provider timeouts, verifier timeouts, recovery policy, Mode Pack decisions, and workspace authority inside the Rust runtime while the CLI owns only transport liveness classes.

Assigns advertised mode-list completion and bounded large task-list/JSON projection requirements to finite CLI Product DoD gaps so terminal CLI completion cannot leave visible commands or unbounded output behavior unresolved.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development, runtime_permission_enforcement, and progress_visualization by removing parser and transport precondition blockers to the primary CLI execution path.
answers.new_capability: The CLI can preserve objective text containing --json, --help, -V, or --version after run, and it routes read-only calls and objective execution calls through distinct transport timeout classes.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: The prior parser consumed global options from the full argument list before identifying the command, which could corrupt objective text. A single runtime timeout also blurred short read-only calls with long-running objective execution liveness.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: CLI-4 could accept corrupted objectives or terminate normal runtime execution under read-only timeout semantics, and CLI product completion could later advertise mode list or JSON/list behavior without a finite DoD owner.
answers.non_duplicative: This is a corrective precondition phase, not another execution wrapper. CLI-4 added run dispatch; CLI-4.1 fixes objective boundary and transport semantics required for that dispatch to be safe.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. No runtime JSON-RPC method or protocol semantic is added; existing fixed runtime calls remain the only execution boundary.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. No report, readiness, history, digest, verdict, preview, or summary surface is added.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Runtime semantics are unchanged. User-visible CLI behavior changes by preserving run objective payloads and using semantic transport timeout classes for runtime calls.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless callers can pass general objective text without flag corruption and can rely on objective execution not being governed by the short read-only liveness timeout.
answers.milestone_progress: Unblocks CLI-4 phase completion review and fixes CLI-6/CLI-7/CLI-8 acceptance ownership before later CLI Product DoD convergence.

accepted_capability: CLI objective parsing now treats tokens after run as payload rather than global CLI options, preserving general objective text for runtime-owned execution.
CLI runtime transport now classifies short read-only requests separately from long-running objective execution requests while leaving execution policy in Rust runtime.
behavior_evidence: Parser and fake-runtime integration test cases verify --json, --help, -V, and --version are preserved inside run objectives.
Runtime-client unit tests verify read-only and objective-execution timeout classes are distinct.
Integration tests verify objective transport timeout redacts and fails closed without terminal objective judgment.
Phase guards validate the corrective manifest and prevent wrapper-only/product-completion claims.
safety_boundary: No Core Runtime terminal campaign state is reopened or mutated.
No runtime JSON-RPC method, protocol schema, ledger semantic, runtime permission rule, Mode Pack rule, provider rule, verifier rule, or workspace mutation authority is added.
CLI timeout remains a transport/liveness concern and does not own LLM, verifier, recovery, agent-loop, journey, or task completion policy.
CLI does not expose raw prompts, provider responses, file contents, stdout/stderr payloads, commands, environment values, absolute paths, canonical paths, or secrets.
non_goals: No new Product DoD capability is claimed closed by this corrective phase.
No resume implementation, mode-list runtime implementation, pagination API, TUI, REPL, shell integration, plugin system, or packaging release.
No generic RPC passthrough, report, readiness, history, digest, verdict, preview, or summary surface.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected requiring -- as the normal objective boundary because run can own the remaining argument payload after command recognition.
Rejected one shared BROWNIE_RUNTIME_TIMEOUT_MS for read-only and objective execution because it conflates short inspection with long-running transport liveness.
Rejected broad JSON output rewrite in this phase because CLI-7 is the finite owner for stable bounded public JSON projection.
Rejected assigning mode list to a new CLI-11 because existing CLI-6 owns progress/next-action UX and advertised runtime-owned mode visibility.
technical_debt: CLI-7 must replace raw-ish inspect/list JSON result exposure with stable bounded CLI-owned projections.
CLI-6 and CLI-7 must evaluate realistic large task-list fixtures and transport response limit behavior before CLI product completion.
CLI-6 must implement or otherwise resolve advertised brownie mode list through runtime-owned mode information before terminal completion.
next_capability_rationale: After CLI-4.1 lands, CLI-4 phase-complete assessment can close the primary run gap if PR #292 evidence plus this correction remain valid.
CLI-5 should then implement restart-safe brownie resume using runtime-owned progress and replay evidence.
